purpose: Primary-source research context for the expanded VkFFT campaign; paper speedups are not measurements of this repository

sources.title: TurboFFT: Co-Designed High-Performance and Fault-Tolerant Fast Fourier Transform on GPUs
sources.supported_observation: The authors generate parameterized FFT kernels and search kernel parameters; they discuss processing one signal per block for some sizes to improve SM utilization.
sources.our_inference: Batch grouping should remain a joint search variable rather than being fixed while studying radix. This is motivation for testing, not proof of the same mechanism on our RTX 4090.

sources.title: Auto-tuning of Fast Fourier Transform on Graphics Processors
sources.version: PPoPP 2011; historical foundation, not a recent paper
sources.supported_observation: The framework composes kernel variants and prunes the space using compute and memory considerations; its variants include twiddle and I/O choices.
sources.our_inference: Radix and block dimensions alone are not the entire optimization space. LUT and memory-layout choices deserve separately admitted experiments; historical reported speedups cannot be transferred to modern VkFFT.

sources.title: A methodology for comparing optimization algorithms for auto-tuning
sources.supported_observation: The paper distinguishes evaluation count from actual elapsed tuning time and includes setup, stochasticity, stopping and cross-space performance aggregation in its methodology.
sources.our_inference: Report best-so-far curves both by evaluated candidates and by reserved elapsed time. Do not use fewer evaluations as evidence of lower total search cost, or a temporary plateau as proof of a global optimum.
